podcast.title: Polaris Music Prize Nomination (2006)
podcast.body: The New Pornographers were nominated for the first Polaris Music Prize in 2006, where their record was considered alongside others but did not win, with Final Fantasy taking the prize. "The winning album was... By Final Fantasy... which won out over records by Broken Social Scene, The New Prenogpers, and Metric."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Formation and Indie Label Partnership
podcast.body: Formed in Vancouver in 1997, the band began releasing albums through the indie label Mint Records starting in 2000. Their success provided significant momentum for the broader indie scene. "They were formed in Vancouver in 1997 and started releasing albums through Mint and 2000."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: International Critical Acclaim
podcast.body: *Mass Romantic* garnered high ratings in international year-end critics polls, including Rolling Stone magazine, which further boosted the visibility of the indie universe. "It was also voted up high in a variety of international year end critics polls including Rolling Stone."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Juno Award for Alternative Album
podcast.body: Their debut album, *Mass Romantic*, won the Alternative Juno Award, signifying critical recognition in Canada. "That first record won the alternative Juno."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Kurt Dahle Joining
podcast.body: Kurt Dahle, previously a member of Age of Electric and Limblifter, joined The New Pornographers. This move marked a significant career transition for Dahle into another prominent Canadian musical group. "Kurt left to join the new pornographers."

podcast.title: Vancouver Origins
podcast.body: The New Pornographers are noted as a band from Vancouver, who, by recording for Mint Records, played a role in advancing the cause for all indie bands in the earliest years of the 21st century. "From Vancouver, mass pornographers, recording for the indie label Mint Records, and advancing the cause for all indie bands in the earliest years of the 21st century."

xref.title: Lineup Change and Continued Activity
xref.body: Kurt Dahle left Limblifter to join The New Pornographers, while Ryan Dahle continued with Limblifter. This change illustrates the dynamic nature of band memberships in the Canadian music landscape, with Ryan Dahle remaining active in the project. "Kurt left to join the new pornographers, where Ryan stayed behind in Limlifter."
